title: Normalized direct-image and open-extension compositors
statement: Use values of finite words [def-pur-compact-scalar-site-words] and normalized inverse-image squares [def-pur-normalized-inverse-image-square]. The paste of two inverse-image identifications is defined using whiskering and functor associators. A composition identification for composable squares p,q and their composite square r consists of inverse-image compositors on set sheaves in both systems, satisfying their composition cube with the vertical set comparisons, and four ordinary module inverse-image compositors whose images under the underlying-sheaf functors are precisely those set compositors. A direct letter retains one inverse-image square and its four direct models. An isomorphism comparison of word values is four actual natural isomorphisms, with its underlying comparison given by their hom transformations. Define the direct-image compositor R_q R_p≅R_r as the adjunction conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the exact descended inverse-image compositor, composed with the exact-derived-functor compositor. Define the open-extension compositor by the inverse-direction adjunction conjugate of the same restriction compositor under the open adjunctions. These definitions fix the counit and open-unit normalization; their site-square equations are not part of the data.
